full_judgment:
4. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that suit is bad for defect of parties and barred in the present form. The suit land claimed by the plaintiff by auction purchase is correct but statement on possession is not correct that the plaintiffs and the defendants possessed the suit land by an amicable compromise for long time but the same was not partitioned through court, that the defendant No. 1 has been in possession of 2½  decimal in plot No. 690/1224 and defendant No. 2 has been possessing 2½ decimal in plot No. 714 by constructing house thereon. Accordingly, they prayed for separate saham. 

 9. In the appeal, the plaintiffs and the defendants filed solenama and petitioner who did not contest the suit by filing statement did not file any cross appeal was impleaded as respondent No. 3. The deposition of the petitioner was recorded and was allowed to cross examine plaintiff and the defendant after their depositions were recorded by the appellate Court in support of solenama. 

 10. The appellant No. 1 on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants in his deposition stated that they compromised with defendant-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 by solenama. The suit will be decreed in terms of solenama which will be treated as part of the decree. In cross he admitted that they lost in the court below and he is not aware whether trial Court by the judgment and decree discarded and found the papers used by the plaintiffs as complainant filed Criminal Case No. 108/99 and the papers filed in the suit were forged and fabricated. He admitted that the petitioner (respondent No. 3) was in permissive possession on the suit land for 5/6 years. He denied that the petitioner had been residing for 30 years. 

 11. Defendant-respondent No.1 in his deposition corroborated the plaintiff-appellant on compromise for decree in terms of solenama. He stated that he did not reside on the land: The claim in the suit was for 05 stakes in respect of khatian No.677 and no land for any other khatian. He could not say the number of the suit and name of learned Advocate who conducted his case. He denied that the suit was filed to grab the land of Anowara (petitioner) which she got by gift from Sarajini. 

 12. The petitioner in her deposition stated that she resided on the land of plot No.690/ 1240 khatian No.677 with her son and daughter. She had house on the land, she used to serve in the residence of Sarajini as domestic aid being pleased she gifted the land to her. She was not impleaded as party and if she was aware about the suit she would have contested. 

 13. On consideration of certified copies of Bainama, writ of delivery of possession and the service return on the delivery of possession of the Rent Decree Execution Case Nos.754/54 and 4/69 filed by the plaintiff in the suit marked Exhibits 2-2/Ga, the learned trial Court held that in Rent Decree Execution Case No.4 of 1960 the name of decree holder. Bank of Calcutta, represented by the Manager and in the Rent Decree Execution Case No.754 of 1954 the name of decree holder Thakur Estate, represented by Sree Babu Usha Ranjan Ganguly are mentioned. As the auction is for arrear rent of land in SA plot No. and SA Khatian the rent fallen arrear must be on account of the Government and, as such, naturally after the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act Part V came into force Government should have been decree holder of the rent decree Execution case or any person duly authorised by the Government. Since the matter is otherwise, it aroused suspicion. It is further held on careful observation of the papers (Exhibits 2-2ga) it reveals that the stamp papers used in the certified copies have been fraudulently manufactured by using some old used stamp paper and washing out the writings thereon with the help of chemical substances heat of fire by using rubbish in artificial manner and writing and putting seal and signature thereon subsequently. For, although those certified copies were issued about 40 years back the seals used appear crystal clear of most recent origin. The first page of Exhibit 2 is seen burnt out at one place due to heat of fire and in the last page of Exhibit 2/KA Rent Decree Execution Case No.754 of 1954 some previous writing were distinctly visible, on the 1st page of Exhibit 2/Kha on left hand corner over the stamp of the writ of deli-very the specimen mark of previously affixed seal was still found visible distinctly and over the same the figure "4" of the year 1954 and figure "3" in between the date 31-3-55 was found written up after rubbing. In the same way, the specimen of the seal previously used on the left corner of Exhibit 2/ga was almost distinctly visible. Moreover, in the round seal of Munsif Court the word 'Monsif' is wrongly spelt and word 'Bakaganj' is spelt instead of Munsif and Bakerganj causing suspicion about the seal. The learned trial Court further held since papers filed have been created falsely and fraudulently in support of the title claimed by the plaintiff for the purpose of the suit and though alleged auction purchase is admitted by the defendant in order to enjoy the advantage of the suit it does not establish the claim of the plaintiff, rather it appears to the learned trial Court that suit has been instituted to grab the property of the members of Hindu community. Moreover, had the property been purchased in 1961. or before the plaintiffs should have proved payment of rent by filing rent receipt and steps for alleged mutation and separation of Jama in the name of plaintiffs and defendants in due course and this being not done, the manufactured papers filed do not establish any right title of the plaintiffs and dependents over the suit land and they are not entitled to get decree for partition in respect of separate saham. The learned trial Court in dismissing the suit directed not to issue certified copies of the Exhibits-2-2ka /ga and return of the Exhibits and initiate criminal proceeding under Section 476 of the Code of Criminal Proceeding. 

 16. Ongoing through the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and the relevant certified copies, it appears that the certified copies of bainama, writ of delivery and service return, Exhibits 2-2/ga are the papers whereby both plaintiffs and the defendants claimed their title and possession on the suit land by virtue of auction purchase in the aforesaid Rent Decree Execution Case Nos. 754 of 1954 and 4 of 1960 of the Court of 2nd Munsif. The case of the plaintiffs in the plaint is that Surajini held title and possession in the land of SA khatian No.677 and Sabitri Sundari was the recorded owner and possessor of the land in SA Khatian No.689 which is admitted in the written statement filed by the defendant but plaintiffs filed certified copy of SA Khatian No.689 in the name of Sabitri Sundari marked Exhibit 1 No certified copy of SA Khatian No.677 in the name Sorajini was filed by the plaintiff at the trial. The trial Court held that right title of said Sarojini cannot be presumed only because of admission by the defendant, inasmuch as defendant is an interested party. As auction sale land of SA khatian land took place in 1954 and 1960 for arrear rent after State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force and Part V was finally published, Government or any person duly authorised should have been decree holder giving rise to suspicion. The discussion and finding that Exhibits 2-2ga were written on previously used stamps and signed and sealed and fraudulently manufactured after washing and removing the previous-writings with help of chemical substances by giving hit of fire and spraying dirt superficially, that though the certified copies were issued 40 years before seal used appeared clear and fresh of recent origin with clear distinct and visible marks of subsequent overwriting, manipulation and interpolation on 2ka, 2kha and 2ga in execution case of 1954, figure 4 and figure 3 of the date 31-3-55 after rubbing marks of previous seal, the term 'Munsif' misspelt as 'Monsif' and 'Bakagonj' written in the seal in Exhibits 2, 2ka leading the trial Court to hold that only to grab the property left by the member of Hindu community plaintiffs and the defendant jointly brought the suit and that had the property been acquired by auction purchase in 1961 or before they would naturally take active step for mutation and separation of jama to obtain mutated khatian and rent receipt but no such step was taken, are, in my view, cogent and consistent with materials and evidence and the above findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record and the learned Subordinate Judge as last court of fact without adverting to the fact, and circumstances and setting aside the same on consideration of evidence, acted illegally with material irregularity in decreeing the suit occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is not sustainable and liable to be set aside. I further hold that the trial Court requires no expert opinion in support of such finding on the basis of evidence. The finding of the Court of appeal below that no evidence was adduced for discarding the Exhibits 2-2ka /ga as fraudulently manufactured is unwarranted and is without any legal basis. The Exhibits 2- 2/ ga filed apparently show that it is a collusive suit filed on the basis of fraudulently manufactured papers and in view of the findings of the trial Court the depositions of the plaintiff, appellant and respondents 1-2 recorded by the appellate Court which is contradictory to each other, the preliminary decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge on the basis of sole-nama is not maintainable.
